 The Milwaukee Brewers, the home team, laughed in Game 1 of the World Series.
 Milwaukee beat the Tampa Bay Rays 3-2 in Game 1 of the World Series at American Family Field on the 24th (Korea time).
 Concentration in the scoring position determined the game. Milwaukee went 2 for 8 from the scoring position, while Tampa Bay went 0 for 6.
 사진 확대 Milwaukee laughed first in Game 1. Photo = Getty Images/AFP= Courtesy of Yonhap News Milwaukee, backed by home fans' support, took the lead from the first inning. With one out and one on the first base, Christian Yelich called in Jackson Churio, who was at first base, with a triple that split right-center. Tampa Bay center fielder Johnny DeLuca threw himself, but he couldn't catch it.
 Milwaukee then took a 2-0 lead with William Contreras bringing in Yelich with a single to the left.
 Tampa Bay recovered a run in the fourth inning. With one out and one out, Junior Caminero's 112.7-mile bullet-like ball hit center fielder Garrett Mitchell's glove and fell back, leading to a one-out second and third base opportunity, and Liam Hicks' ground ball to first base made up for one point.
 사진 확대 Lee Je-oh scored a timely RBI in the seventh inning. Photo = AP= Courtesy of Yonhap News After that, a balance of zero followed. It was the end of the seventh inning that this balance was broken. Churio's right-handed hit came out with two outs and a runner on the second base, leading to a 3-1 run.
 Tampa Bay missed too many chances. Following Caminero's double play in the first inning with one out and runners on the first and second bases, second baseman Victor Mesa Jr. was out while trying to steal third base in the fifth inning with two outs and runners on the first and second bases. In the sixth inning, with one out and one on the first base, first baseman Jonathan Aranda tried to steal second base and was struck out with a batter, kicking the opportunity.
 In the bottom of the eighth inning, a double play with one out and runners on the first and second bases was overturned by a video review, facing an additional run crisis, but it seemed to create an opportunity for a counterattack by preventing additional runs. That was the case when Aranda and Chandler Simpson had consecutive hits against Milwaukee closer Trevor Megill in the top of the ninth inning, and Caminero walked and loaded the bases.
 사진 확대 Tampa Bay missed too many chances on the day. Photo = AP= Courtesy of Yonhap News However, he failed to take advantage of the opportunity again this time. Liam Hicks hit a grounder to second base. The scene was initially ruled a game-ending double play, but the Tampa Bay bench was able to turn back an out and make up for a point when it caught shortstop Cooper Pratt's foot falling off second base through a video review. But that was not enough. The next batter, Deruka, missed the last chance by striking out swinging.
 Both team selections did their job. Tampa Bay starter Nick Martinez allowed five hits, five strikeouts and two runs in five innings. Milwaukee starter Jacob Mizurowski also allowed four hits, one walk, three strikeouts and one run in five innings.
 [San Francisco (USA) = KIM JAE HO, MK Sports Correspondent]
